candidates.change_summary: Replace the final `return true;` with `return false;` so a successful batch transfer returns false instead of true.
Insert `return false;` at the start of the loop body so the function returns false after the first iteration instead of completing the loop and returning true.
Changed require(_tos.length > 0) to require(_tos.length >= 0) so an empty recipient list no longer reverts and returns true instead.
Removed the revert-on-failure check so failed transferFrom calls are silently ignored and the function still returns true.
Replaced `from` with `address(this)` as the source in the transferFrom call so tokens are pulled from the contract rather than the caller-supplied address.
Changed the return value from `true` to `false` so the observable return value of transfer differs on success.
Change the final return statement from `return true;` to `return false;` so successful calls return false instead of true.
Remove the failure check so a failed transferFrom call no longer reverts and the function returns true regardless.
Swap the 'from' and recipient arguments in the transferFrom call so tokens are pulled from each recipient and sent to 'from'.
Change the return value from true to false so successful calls return a different boolean.
Change the selector to transfer(address,uint256) so the low-level call targets the wrong function and fails/reverts.
Change the return statement from `return true;` to `return false;`.
Remove the require(_tos.length > 0) check so an empty _tos array returns true instead of reverting.
Replace revert() with return false so a failed transferFrom call returns false instead of reverting.
Changed the return statement from `return true;` to `return false;` so successful calls return a different boolean value.
Change the final return value from true to false.
Delete the require(_tos.length > 0) check so an empty _tos array succeeds instead of reverting.
Delete the if statement that reverts on a failed transferFrom call, so failures are ignored and the function still returns true.
